title: Really not a single negative thing to say about Caroline! Loved this ...
transcript: Chloe Grace-Moretz is starring in one of my favorite plays of the year so far about a young mother with a trans daughter it's deeply absorbing to the point where I almost sometimes forgot that I was watching a play while also packing a huge emotional punch I have to admit I'm usually not a fan of stories that deal with the topic of addiction which is a central part of this play's subject matter as well but the playwright Preston Max Allen consistently approaches it in a way that avoids many of the stale tropes and cliches and I think you can say the same thing about a lot of the thematic territory that the play covers like the play feels in many ways like a traditional drama but the playwright just kept surprising me at every turn with how he manages to maintain a sense of tension and pain hand in hand with a refreshing sense of optimism it's a play where all three characters are beautifully written to the point where even when they are in intense conflict with each other you really see both sides of it and in some ways agree with both of them and meanwhile you can feel that under the surface there is a deep sense of love between all of them the acting was incredibly strong all around it was great to see Chloe Grace-Moretz on stage but I think I was most impressed with the child actor playing Caroline who was very naturalistic but also had this organic charisma and stage presence that really won everyone over I was really just so impressed and moved by this whole project if you're able to catch it I highly recommend doing so it's running at MCC through November 16th
